attribution.note: Marcus states both clauses in his own voice; neither is attributed to another speaker.

semantics.note: The sentence presents cash consumption and investor dissatisfaction as current facts supporting the surrounding speculation about the bid's subtext.

contract.note: The cash-consumption definition and material-investor reading are ordinary and fair. Calendar 2024 is a reasonable supplied convention, though not explicit in the statement. The accounting-basis requirement limits resolution.

evidence.note: Contemporaneous company disclosure supports investor demand for structural changes. It is not an independent finding or proof of opposition to every nonprofit role.
Accurately described secondary reporting covers only the first half of 2024. It cannot establish the contract's full-year cash result.
Published before the evaluation cutoff and referring to full-year 2024, but the reproduced commentary supplies no identifiable cash-flow basis or reconciliation sufficient under the contract.

reviews.rationale: The investor clause has support from OpenAI's disclosure. The cash clause remains unsettled under the contract: the half-year report covers a different period, and the full-year report lacks the required accounting basis. No comparable contrary financial evidence is supplied.
